topic.title: Random Walk
topic.description: A turtle that moves in random directions (up, down, left, right) producing an unpredictable colored path. Introduces algorithmic randomness in graphics.

learningNotes.whatILearned: The same walk in a different shape — a `while` loop with a counter instead of a `for` loop.
learningNotes.challenges: The counter is the only thing keeping the loop finite, and nothing says so; the commented-out block is a different program left in the file.
learningNotes.nextSteps: Delete the commented-out experiment or move it to its own file, and comment the loop bound.

files.description: Random walk turtle with predefined color list.

misconceptions: A `while` loop needs something to stop it — here it is `i < 200`, and the increment has to be inside the loop or it never ends
Half a file of commented-out code is a file where two different programs are arguing with each other
engine.review:
**The rubric I used**

There is no task sheet for this one — it was written before the engine
existed, so there was nothing to grade it against. I graded the file on the
three things that have always mattered here:

- **40 — it runs.** It compiles or interprets without an error.
- **30 — it is right.** The output is what it claims to produce.
- **30 — it explains itself.** Comments say *why*, not *what*.

**0 + 30 + 0 = 30%**

**This file cannot be run here.** It needs `tkinter`, and this
machine has no display and no `tkinter` — so the 40 points for *it runs* are
not ones I can give, and they are not given. The other two bands are judged
by reading the code, carefully, line by line.

There is a bigger point here, and it is worth saying plainly: **`tkinter`
does not exist on Termux either.** These files cannot be run on the phone
this whole system is built around. They are not broken — they are stranded.

**What is right, by reading**

The loop is sound. `i` starts at 0, the body runs, and `i+=1` at the end of the body takes it to 200 — the increment is inside the loop, which is the thing that has to be true or the program never ends. `turtle.done()` keeps the window open.

**What is not**

**A quarter of the file is commented out.** There is a whole alternative version of the movement logic — forward or backward, turn left or right — sitting in comments, and it is a *different* program from the one that runs. A reader cannot tell which one is the real design.

Also `t.pensize(15)` and `t.color(...)` are inside the loop, so they are set two hundred times when once would do. Harmless, but it says the loop was written without a picture of what the loop was for.

**The one thing to fix first**

Take the commented-out version out of the file and give it its own name, or delete it. Then:

```python
while i < 200:  # The counter is the only thing that ends this loop.
```
